newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq asks U.N. to act on Turk troops in north Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Iraq asks U.N. to act on Turk troops in north Iraq.

text.p: The ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra on Monday urged the United Nations to take an action to force Turkish troops in northern Iraq to leave the area.

"Denunciation alone will not be enough to force Turkey to withdraw its invasion troops from Iraqi territories. What is needed is a stronger attitude, more determined, more decisive from the United Nations which will force Turkey to reconsider its stand and pull out its troops," Thawra said in a commentary.

It said all Gulf War U.N. resolutions called for respect of Iraqi sovereignty and territorial integrity. "What has the U.N. done in the face of this flagrant violation of Iraqi sovereignty and the integrity of its land and air space?" the paper asked.
"The U.N. is required to assume a more powerful and more effective role to restrain Turkey, which is perpetrating an aggressive action against Iraq," it said.

Thousands of Turkish troops backed by artillery, armour and helicopter gunships have consolidated their position in northern Iraq after a 12-day-old foray in pursuit of separatist guerrillas of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
